entry.title: Conditional Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
entry.summary: We study conditional denoising diffusion models for probabilistic forecasting of multivariate time series. The model learns to reverse a gradual noising process while conditioning on the observed history, and produces calibrated forecast distributions on six public benchmarks.

entry.title: Score-Based Imputation of Missing Values in Multivariate Time Series
entry.summary: Missing values are common in sensor and clinical time series. We propose a score-based diffusion model that imputes missing entries by conditioning on the observed values, and show that it outperforms deterministic imputation methods on air quality and healthcare datasets.

entry.title: Diffusion Transformers for Long-Horizon Time Series Forecasting
entry.summary: Long-horizon forecasting requires models that capture both trend and seasonality over hundreds of steps. We combine a transformer backbone with a diffusion objective and report lower forecasting error than autoregressive transformers on electricity, traffic and weather benchmarks.

entry.title: Denoising Diffusion for Anomaly Detection in Sensor Time Series
entry.summary: We detect anomalies in industrial sensor time series by measuring how well a denoising diffusion model reconstructs each window. Windows with high reconstruction error are flagged as anomalous, giving strong detection results on three public anomaly detection benchmarks.

entry.title: A Survey of Diffusion Models for Time Series Analysis
entry.summary: This survey reviews diffusion models for time series, covering forecasting, imputation, generation and anomaly detection. We organise more than one hundred papers by conditioning strategy and network architecture, and list open problems for the field.

entry.title: Autoregressive Denoising Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
entry.summary: We propose an autoregressive model that uses denoising diffusion at each time step to sample from the conditional distribution of the next value. The approach gives sharp probabilistic forecasts for high-dimensional multivariate series.

entry.title: Latent Diffusion for Irregularly Sampled Clinical Time Series
entry.summary: Clinical measurements are recorded at irregular intervals. We encode irregular observations into a continuous latent space and train a latent diffusion model there, improving imputation and mortality prediction on intensive care records.

entry.title: Generating Synthetic Financial Time Series with $\mathcal{O}(T)$ Diffusion Sampling
entry.summary: We generate synthetic financial time series with a diffusion sampler whose cost grows linearly with the series length. Generated price paths keep the heavy tails and volatility clustering of real markets, with a discriminative score gap of <5%, which makes them useful for risk and R&D teams that cannot share real data.

entry.title: Stochastic Processes for Sequence Modelling: A Diffusion Perspective
entry.summary: We view sequence modelling through stochastic differential equations and describe how diffusion processes can model the evolution of time series. The note connects classical filtering with modern generative models.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Diffusion Models for Spatio-Temporal Weather Series
entry.summary: We add physical constraints from the governing equations to a diffusion model for spatio-temporal weather series. The constrained model produces ensembles that respect conservation laws and improves medium-range forecast skill over an unconstrained baseline.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain Diffusion for Time Series Generation
entry.summary: We run the diffusion process on Fourier coefficients instead of raw values. Generating time series in the frequency domain preserves periodic structure and improves the realism of generated samples.

entry.title: Benchmarking Diffusion Models Against Transformers for Traffic Forecasting
entry.summary: We compare diffusion models and transformers for traffic forecasting on four road sensor networks under a shared evaluation protocol. Diffusion models give better calibrated uncertainty, while transformers remain faster and slightly more accurate for point forecasts.
